paragraphs.text: Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani announced the policy change during a cabinet briefing on Wednesday.
The original Agniveer Yojana was announced in June 2022.
The Agnipath scheme, launched in June 2022, recruits soldiers for a four-year term with 25 per cent retained in regular service.
A maximum of 25 percent of Agniveers can be included in the regular cadre based on organizational needs and selection processes.
On Wednesday, the Union Cabinet approved a change to the Agnipath Yojana.
Central Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani announced the cabinet decision at the National Media Centre.
On Thursday, the Janata Dal (United) welcomed the government's decision to provide a two-year extension to Agniveers.
Rajeev Ranjan Prasad described the extension as a "wonderful Diwali gift" for Agniveers.
"The Modi government is scared," co-convener of the Cockroach Janata Party said.
"Agniveers who are not retained after the six-year service period will not receive reservation in any government job," Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani said.
"Extending the Agniveer Yojana by two years does not address its fundamental flaws," Retired Lieutenant Colonel N. N Tyagarajan said.
Approximately 18,300 Agniveers were scheduled to exit the armed forces by 31 December.
Agniveers leaving after six years were not entitled to pension, gratuity, or ex-servicemen medical and canteen facilities.
The Agnipath Yojana does not apply to officer ranks.

other_coverage.text: Agniveers are not entitled to dearness allowance or military service pay.
The Agnipath Yojana is a recruitment scheme for soldiers, airmen, and sailors in the three wings of the Indian Armed Forces, launched about four years ago.
The government introduced the Agnipath Yojana for military recruitment.
Agniveers receive a lump sum Seva Nidhi package after completing four years of service.
The Seva Nidhi package is exempt from income tax.
Agniveers who complete four years of service are not entitled to pension and gratuity.
Agniveers are provided with a non-contributory life insurance cover of 48 lakh rupees during their four-year service.
The Ministry of Home Affairs reserved 50 percent of vacancies for former Agniveers in Central Armed Police Forces and Assam Rifles in July 2026.
Indian Railways has reserved 10 percent of vacancies for former Agniveers in Level-1 posts and 5 percent in Level-2 and above posts.
Agniveers selected for the regular cadre must serve a minimum of 15 years and become eligible for pension and other service benefits under regular soldier rules.
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship has agreements with NIOS and IGNOU to provide Agniveers opportunities to complete 10th, 12th, and graduation studies.
